summary: CRACKED the FORCE/PICK/EXIT door menu. KEY CORRECTION TO PRIOR SPIKES: FUN_0000_9345 (currently MISLABELED 'save_load_menu' in Ghidra) IS the door FORCE/PICK/EXIT menu, NOT a save/load UI. It is reached from FUN_0000_95ba's TYPE-7 special-record branch (call 0x92ea->0x9345 at file 0x9603), and the type-7 record is the door. (0x95ba's type-3 branch is the chest -> 0x9532, confirmed.) The OPEN command path is: dungeon main loop -> dungeon_in_camp_menu (0x2794) PARTY OPTIONS grid -> grid index 4 (case handler 0x294b) -> call FUN_0000_95ba -> for the special record AT THE PARTY CELL, type 7 -> call FUN_0000_9345 (door menu). The menu shows FORCE/PICK/EXIT (indexedMessage ids 0x834/0x835/0x836) via menu_grid_select (0x1574) at file 0x947f. FORCE (case 0) calls FUN_0000_8974; PICK (case 1) calls FUN_0000_8e4f (both currently mislabeled rest_save/load_session). Both first prompt WHO WILL TRY? (indexedMsg id 0x83e) via the member picker 0x9c8 + party_check_member_alive (0x2086), then run an animated strain/tumble bar, roll vs the door's lock field, and print success(0x841)/failure(0x842)/jammed(0x843). On success they open the door by clearing the special-record's +0x240 wall-plane bit for the current facing (FUN_0000_88af) -- they do NOT auto-step the party through. The +0x834..+0x843 ids map exactly to the task's indexedMessages 534..542 (FORCE..jammed), proving the identity.

findings.claim: SPECIAL-RECORD TABLE LAYOUT (HIGH CONFIDENCE — pinned from live save-1 reads + disassembly). base = DGROUP near-pointer at [0x4fa8] = 0x8184 in save-1 (physical: DGROUP+0x8184 = phys 0x201cc). Max 144 (0x90) records (si = 0..0x8f in 366e). All coordinate/type/lock fields are BYTE arrays (stride 1, index=recidx). Wall-plane is a WORD array (stride 2, index=recidx*2 — confirmed by 'D1E6 shl si,1' before '[bx+si+0x240]' in wmaze 0x961c/0x8ad7). Field offsets from base: (1) +0x360 TYPE byte — 3=chest, 7=door (other types also exist: 1,4,5,6,8,11,16,19,21,23,24,25). (2) +0x3f0 X coord byte (zone-local column 0..7). (3) +0x480 Y coord byte (zone-local row 0..7). (4) +0x510 Z/region byte (0..11). (5) +0x240 WALL-PLANE word (2 bytes/record, LE; getbit_chunk extracts 2-bit facing value at bit offset = facing*2, LSB-first): value 0=open, 1=closed, 2=welded. (6) +0x630 LOCK byte (getbit_chunk width=5, offset=0 -> 5-bit strength 0..31). (7) +0x6c0 PER-REGION FIRST-RECORD-INDEX byte array (12 bytes, indexed by region/z = [0x4f9c]; gives the scan start index for 366e). (8) +0x120 unknown WORD per record (read in FORCE setup at 8ad7 with recidx*2, purpose unconfirmed — may be a door-name or UI string pointer). CONFIRMED from live reads of phys arrays in save-1: type array at DGROUP+0x84e4 (phys 132396), x at DGROUP+0x8574 (phys 132540), y at DGROUP+0x8604 (phys 132684), z at DGROUP+0x8694 (phys 132828), lock at DGROUP+0x87b4 (phys 133116), per-region at DGROUP+0x8844 (phys 133260). getbit_chunk (wroot image 0x2962, thunk 0xe3fe) confirmed = (data>>offset)&mask with LSB-first bit ordering.

evidence.details: Save-1 DGROUP reads (phys base 0x18048): [0x4fa8]=0x8184 (base ptr). Type array at DGROUP+0x84e4 (bx+0x360): record 109=0x07 (DOOR), records 95/98/112/136/143=0x03 (CHESTs). x at DGROUP+0x8574: rec109=7. y at DGROUP+0x8604: rec109=0. z at DGROUP+0x8694: rec109=4. per-region at DGROUP+0x8844: [7]=0x79=121 (region 7 starts at record 121). Lock at DGROUP+0x87b4: rec109=0x00 (5-bit lock=0). Wall at DGROUP+0x83c4 (WORD array, stride 2): rec109 at offset 109*2=218 = phys 132326 = bytes[0x00,0x08] -> word 0x0800. getbit_chunk at wroot image 0x2962 (thunk 0xe3fe): 'shr bx,cl; mask=(0xffff>>(16-width)); return (data>>offset)&mask' — LSB-first. 366e (wmaze file 0x366e): scans si from specialIdx (+0x6c0[z]) to 0x8f, checks [bx+si+0x510]==z AND [bx+si+0x3f0]==x AND [bx+si+0x480]==y AND type!=0 AND 0xe34b level-filter; returns si (recidx) on match or 0xffff. Force setup at 8ae6: 'mov si,[bp+6]; mov al,[bx+si+0x630]' — BYTE access, stride 1. Wall at 8ad7: 'shl ax,1; mov si,ax; mov ax,[bx+si+0x240]' — WORD access, stride 2.

findings.claim: THE LEVEL-0 DOOR: record 109 is the SOLE type-7 door in the level-0 special-record table. Coordinates: z=4 (region 4, gxBase=120, gyBase=132), x=7, y=0. Global: gx=127, gy=132. In save-1: lock_byte=0x00 (5-bit lock strength=0, trivially easy to force/pick — consistent with a castle entry door that the game expects players to simply open). Wall word=0x0800 in save-1 (getbit_chunk at facing*2=4 = 0 = open state — door may have been opened prior to this save). The 366e lookup for region 7 (party in B1 area of level-0) starts at record 121 and finds records 121-124 (all type 1/16/19/21, not type 7). The only type-7 door is in region 4 (surface/castle area). PARTY-POSITION CAVEAT: save-1 party coords are z=7,x=3,y=2 (region 7, B1 area), which does NOT match the door at z=4,x=7,y=0. The FORCE/PICK menu was active when this save was taken; the party coords reflect the position at save time, not necessarily the position when OPEN was originally pressed. The mismatch is documented but not resolved — possible causes: (a) save was taken while inside 9345 menu after the party navigated away, (b) z=[0x4f9c] tracks a different coordinate than maze-block region, (c) the door approach is from a neighboring region. For the decoder purpose, the door record IS at record 109 in the table.

evidence.details: Type array scan (DGROUP+0x84e4, 144 bytes): only record 109 = 0x07. Records 121-124 (region 7, z=7): types 1,16,19,21 (no door). Record 109 z=4,x=7,y=0 -> global gx=gxBase[4]+7=127, gy=gyBase[4]+0=132 (gxBase[4]=120, gyBase[4]=132 from extracted/maze/level-0.json mazeBlock). Lock: DGROUP+0x87b4[109]=0x00 -> strength=0. Wall: DGROUP+0x83c4[109*2..109*2+1]=[0x00,0x08]=word 0x0800; getbit_chunk(0x0800,4,2)=0 (open). Party in save-1: z=[0x4f9c]=7, y=[0x4f9e]=2, x=[0x4fa0]=3, facing=[0x4f9a]=2. Door at (z=4,x=7,y=0) facing=? (approach direction not confirmed). recommend_check: read party coords at the moment OPEN is pressed (requires live instrumentation) to confirm the door approach direction and whether facing=2 (south) corresponds to the south wall of cell (4,7,0).

findings.claim: CORRECTION to live-door-level0-record109 / the Task-1.4 decoder: the ENTRANCE/starting level's special-record block is scenario.dbs bank-3 RECORD 0 (base 0xe828 + 0*0x6cc), NOT record 12. Record 0 holds 12 type-7 (forceable/pickable) doors with locks 3..7; record 12 holds only the single lock-0 castle-entry door (recidx 109) and was the WRONG block. Validated by mapping rec0's type-7 records through level-0's gxBase/gyBase (from extracted/maze/level-0.json): e.g. rec0 recidx 24 -> global (124,121), lock 3, closed on facing 2 -- which is exactly the door reached by the user's path from the start gate (turn-left, forward x3, turn-left). The symmetric door rec0 recidx 42 -> (130,121) lock 3. Other entrance doors: (124,123)L3,(130,123)L3,(124,129)L3,(124,131)L3,(125,130)L3,(129,130)L3,(130,129)L3,(130,131)L3. ALL starting-area doors are forceable type-7 records, confirming the user's recollection. The detection RE (0x95ba type-7 record at party cell -> 0x9345 FORCE/PICK menu) is CORRECT; only the bank-3 record SELECTION in the decoder was wrong. NOTE: the 'ceiling[zone]=bank3 rec(zone+2)' formula is for the CEILING image asset and is NOT the special-record mapping; the special-record table for level N is bank-3 record N (rec0 for the entrance level). type-7 records in bank-3 records >=20 have garbage coords (z/x/y out of range) -- those records are non-maze (item/monster) data, so the level->record mapping must be bounded to real maze levels.

evidence.details: Scan of all bank-3 records (base 0xe828, recsize 0x6cc) counting type bytes ==7 at +0x360+recidx: rec0=12 doors, rec1=16, rec2=9, rec5=8, rec12=1 (the wrongly-selected block). rec0 doors mapped via level-0.json gxBase=[120,128,120,128,120,128,...] gyBase=[116,116,124,124,132,132,...]: recidx24 z0 x4 y5 -> (124,121) lock3 wall0x10 (closed facing2); recidx42 z1 x2 y5 -> (130,121) lock3. Matches user path turn-left/fwd*3/turn-left from entrance (127,121).

unresolved_updated_by_pass3: PARTY-COORD/DOOR-RECORD MISMATCH: save-1 party is at z=7,x=3,y=2 but the type-7 door is at z=4,x=7,y=0. These are in different maze regions (region 7 = B1 area, region 4 = castle surface). Unresolved. Best guess: save was taken inside the 9345 menu, and the party had moved since OPEN was pressed (or z=[0x4f9c] encodes something other than the maze-block region for the door area).

DOOR APPROACH FACING: which facing value (0-3) does the party use when approaching the level-0 castle door at (z=4,x=7,y=0)? The wall word 0x0800 has getbit_chunk(offset=facing*2) = 0 for facing 0..4, so if the door IS open in the save, we can't determine the closed-state facing from this snapshot alone. Need a fresh save while the door is closed.

+0x120 WORD ARRAY: the FORCE function reads a WORD at [bx+recidx*2+0x120] at 8adf before the lock read. Purpose unknown (may be door-title string offset or visual index). Record 109's +0x120 word = bytes[8adf read not performed]. Not needed for basic decoder but should be identified.

The door LOCK-STRENGTH source: both FORCE and PICK read getbit_chunk(width=5, off=0) of the record's +0x630 byte ([bp-4]). I have NOT confirmed +0x630 is the lock-difficulty field vs a door-message id (in 0x95ba/0x9345 +0x630 byte is also copied to *0x43c4 message field elsewhere). Decode +0x630 across known easy vs hard doors live and confirm the 5-bit lock value drives strain-length / tumbler-count.

Char-struct field identities (offsets are absolute BSS = roster_base + member*0x1b0 + struct_rel; struct_rel = abs - 0x4404 for member 0): FORCE stat +0x4514 (struct-rel 0x110) -- presumed STRENGTH but UNVERIFIED; PICK skill +0x440c (rel 0x8) + +0x452b (rel 0x127) -- presumed PICK-LOCKS skill (current + bonus) but UNVERIFIED; class +0x4587 (rel 0x183) confirmed-as-class via wpcvw-skill-action.json. +0x4404 (rel 0) / +0x4406 (rel 2) used in the FORCE roll as a stamina/HP ratio -- identity unverified. Map all five via dosbox_read_struct against a known character sheet.

Exact success comparator: FORCE outcome is decided by JL at 0x8da9 (strain progress [bp-0x3a] < strain length [bp-0x38] => success). But a separate roll [bp-6] (stamina*stat/maxstamina) is also computed and gates an early-failure RNG path (c47e(0x32)) at 0x8c56. Whether [bp-6]<=0 forces failure independent of the bar, and the exact JL/JG directions, are LOW confidence -- live-verify.

Whether a FAILED FORCE/PICK writes any persistent door state (so a door can become permanently jammed by repeated bad FORCEs). Static read of the failure branch (0x891d) shows only [0x4ee0+facing*2]=0 + record-update + sound, no +0x630/+0x240 writeback -- but confirm live that re-attempting a failed door has identical odds.

The 'USE A KEY' third action from lived recollection: not present as a label in the 9345 FORCE/PICK/EXIT menu (only 3 labels 0x834..0x836). Either keys are handled via OPTIONS USE ITEM (wdopt state 0x14) on a keyed door, or there is a different/larger door menu for keyed doors that this type-7 path does not reach. Drive a KEYED door live to see if a 4th option ('KEY') ever appears or if keyed doors route through USE ITEM.

getbit_chunk (0xe3fe) vs getbits (0xe3c1): the +0x240 reads here use 0xe3fe (width-2 chunk read) and the +0x630 read uses 0xe3fe width-5. Confirm 0xe3fe's exact bit semantics (offset units, MSB/LSB) against a live decode so the TS reimplementation reads the correct lock value.
